My probe with a changed `src/a.js` printed `docs/adr/0001-x.md: Accepted. Affects matches src/a.js.` The new test "review mode with --diff uses all changed files of the diff" fails when I put the old filter back.
- M1, each deleted or renamed ADR fails: **fixed**. The code reads the old Status from the removed lines. A deleted Proposed ADR passed with exit 0. A deleted Accepted ADR failed with exit 1. The comment and the message now say "Accepted". The mutation "each deletion fails" makes 1 test fail.
- M2, no "Consumer action:" line for the number check: **fixed**. The author took the second fix: only a new ADR can fail the shared-number check. Two old ADRs with the number 0001 on `main` passed for an unrelated change. A new ADR with a used number failed. The mutation "check all ADRs" makes 1 test fail. No consumer action is necessary now.
- M3, two mutations survive: **fixed**. Without `--no-renames` in the `-U0` diff, 1 test fails ("with git, renaming an Accepted ADR fails"). Without the removed-lines guard in `statusOnly`, 1 test fails ("a status-only change must not remove other lines").
- L1, content lines that start with "-- " or "++ " are not seen: **fixed**. `parseDiff` now counts the lines of each hunk from the hunk header. My probe that removed `-- note` failed with exit 1.
- L2, the amendment check does not run with `--` and says nothing: **fixed**. The CLI now prints "Amendment check NOT RUN. Give the diff with --diff <file>." Two tests fail when I remove the line.
- L3, the red step failed at import: **open**. The body still says the tests failed at import and the code came first. The body does not say whether the seven new tests were red before the fix.

## New findings

### M4. `--no-renames` in the name list has no test

- `scripts/check-adrs.mjs:255`
- Problem: the delta adds `--no-renames` to `git diff --name-only`. Now the new path of a renamed ADR counts as an added file, so the name check runs on it. My probe renamed a Proposed ADR to `0001_Bad.md`. It failed with the file name error. I removed the flag and ran `test/check-adrs.test.mjs`. All 31 tests passed.
- Rule: [coding/testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/coding/testing.md) and [code-review step 7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/skills/code-review/SKILL.md#7-tests). Each behavior change has a test that fails when the behavior is wrong.
- Why: a later edit can remove the flag, and the gate stays green. A renamed Proposed ADR with a bad name then passes.
- Fix: add a git mode test that renames a Proposed ADR to a bad name and expects the file name error.

### L4. A blank context line without its space breaks the rest of a `--diff` file

- `scripts/check-adrs.mjs:159` to `163`
- Problem: in a hunk, the parser counts only lines that start with "+", "-" or a space. Some tools and editors remove the trailing space of a blank context line. Then the hunk count never reaches 0. The parser reads the next `diff --git` block as part of the first file. My probe with such a diff gave 6 errors on `docs/adr/0001-x.md`. Three errors quoted lines of `docs/adr/0002-y.md` and its header `-- a/docs/adr/0002-y.md`. Git itself always writes the space, so git mode and CI are not affected.
- Rule: [code-review severity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/skills/code-review/SKILL.md#severity). Low, because only a hand-made `--diff` file can have this form.
- Why: the errors name the wrong file and the wrong lines. The old parser was not affected in this way.
- Fix: in a hunk, count an empty line as a context line. Also end the hunk at a line that starts with `diff --git `. Add a test.

## Blast radius

- The one safety fact: the CLI keeps each old option and each old exit code. A consumer CI call with `--base <ref>` still works. Level 4, Run. A repository with no `docs/adr/` folder passed with exit 0. An unrelated change in a repository with old ADRs passed with exit 0.
- Cleared risks: old ADRs that share a number no longer fail a consumer pull request (M2). Deleted and renamed Proposed ADRs follow the documented rule (M1). Git mode is not affected by L4.
- Remaining risk: a consumer that renames a Proposed ADR now gets the name check on the new name. That is the rule in [architecture/adrs.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/architecture/adrs.md#place-and-name), but no test holds it (M4).
